extracted.intended_audience: Prospective AAAI-23 authors, reviewers, and program committee members
extracted.subtask_description: Conference-specific guidelines for submitting papers to AAAI-23 and for their review, covering the two-phase review workflow, double-blind requirements, citation handling, author feedback, and key deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase review: Phase 1 allocation and immediate rejection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper will be allocated two reviewers. If a paper receives two reviews that are both sufficiently negative, it will be rejected without any opportunity for author feedback. Remaining papers will progress to Phase 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1 uses two initial reviewers per submission; dual sufficiently negative reviews trigger summary rejection (no author response opportunity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase review: Phase 2 allocation and independence of initial reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper will be allocated additional reviewers in Phase 2. These reviewers will not be given access to Phase 1 reviews until after submitting their own reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 2 brings extra reviewers who must form their own opinions without seeing Phase 1 reviews first, ensuring independent assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author feedback phase (single feedback window)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single author feedback phase will give authors of papers from Phase 2 an opportunity to comment on all reviews (from both phases), running from October 20-23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may respond to reviewer comments in the specified short window; these comments will be available during subsequent PC/SPC discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program committee and senior program committee discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The program committee and senior program committee will engage in a discussion phase, taking author feedback into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PC/SPC will deliberate on papers after taking the author feedback into account to form final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final decisions announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Final decisions will be announced on November 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect final acceptance/rejection notifications on the specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-23 reviews are double blind (i.e., neither reviewers nor authors should be able to identify each other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be prepared so authors and reviewers cannot identify one another; failure to maintain anonymity may lead to summary rejection at the program chairs' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-page content and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page, on which the paper body begins, should include the title, abstract, content areas, and ID number (if available), but not names or affiliations of the authors. Acknowledgments of funding or assistance should also be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only title/abstract/areas/ID should appear on page one; omit author names, affiliations, and acknowledgments to preserve double-blindness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that no information is included that would identify the authors or their affiliations; papers including such information may be summarily rejected at the discretion of the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must actively remove or anonymize any content (text, metadata, file properties, acknowledgments, figure captions, project URLs, etc.) that could reveal identity or affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to cite relevant published literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should include references to all published literature relevant to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must not omit relevant published work; proper referencing is expected even under anonymity constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite authors' previous work (three options)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the authors’ previous work is relevant, they have three options, in descending order of desirability: (1) Use the third person, rather than the first person. (2) Avoid citing previous, unpublished work that would surely identify the authors; such citations may be added to the camera-ready copy. (3) When neither previous option is appropriate, cite as “Anonymous (2019)” to indicate that a citation has been suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred: refer to own prior work in third-person (e.g., “Previously, Hinton et al (2006) showed...”). If unpublished/identifying material must be cited, defer it to camera-ready. Only use anonymized placeholder citations when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for non-anonymous online material (allowed but must be hidden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two cases where the existence of non-anonymous online material will not be considered a violation: (1) preliminary unrefereed preprints (e.g., arXiv, social media, personal websites) or workshop papers without archival proceedings; (2) research talks (even if abstracts or videos are online).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such non-anonymous material exists, the AAAI-23 submission should not include citations or pointers to it, and the non-anonymous online material should not reference that the work was submitted to AAAI-23; violations may lead to summary rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer guidance on encountering non-anonymous prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be instructed not to actively seek out such previous publications or to share knowledge of them with other reviewers but will not be disqualified if they encounter such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should refrain from searching for or disseminating identifying prior versions; inadvertent discovery does not automatically disqualify the reviewer, but active seeking is discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines (abstract and full paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract deadline for AAAI submissions will be August 8, 2022, and the deadline for full paper submissions will be August 15, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must adhere to the stated deadlines for abstract and full paper submission.
